name: Cameron Kelly
life: “I still remember measuring a sofa in a house I hadn't decided to leave.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Cameron knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I want to downsize while the house is still ours to choose. I've already measured the furniture.
appearance: Cameron has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for silver temples and a dark fringe. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Cameron folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Cameron takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Cameron can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To keep downsizing possible while there is still a choice.
family: Laurence Salcedo is Cameron’s half-sibling. Cameron knows which ones can be shared. Laurence keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *The porch auction*, Laurence says, “I needed somewhere to sit on my way home after surgery.”
connections: Gavin Roche. A loan processed in minutes can undo a downsizing plan worked on for months.

reactions.situation: A sibling wants the bank figures read at a family meal
reactions.response: Cameron asks the guarantor what can be shared at dinner before reading out any figures.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Cameron writes down their exact words with room left for uncertainty and gives them back to check.

reactions.situation: If someone else wins the opportunity
reactions.response: Cameron turns up the next morning with the one piece of advice that would have helped either of them.
